goal.what: Whoever builds or changes Lane, a person or an AI, makes it give the developer AI what it comes for: subagents that keep the rules of their steps, and an orchestrator that starts them as the routes say, on every run, with no check code or script of its own.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json goal: "Whoever builds or changes the product, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for."

.rn/20261013-rebuild/steering.md:76: "Lane's flow becomes routing ... from a declaration of routes (from a role, on a result, to a role) it takes each role's result, tells the next and stops any other start"

questions.what: Reading an objective, does the developer know which user the product is for and what that user gets from it?
Weighing a piece of work, can the developer tell which one objective it brings closer?
After a change, can the developer tell from the key results whether users came closer to the objective?
Weighing a change that shortens the lead time, can the developer tell whether it keeps how well the user gets what the objective says?
For each objective, can the developer follow, step by step, how its user goes from when they first need it to having what the objective says?
Building a step of a scenario, can the developer tell whether it waits for a person, is taken by an AI, or runs as a script?
Can the developer change how the product works inside, while its users see the same, and leave the document as it is?

decisions.what: Who comes to Lane with a goal of their own?
decisions.decided: The developer AI, an AI that builds a Claude Code plugin whose subagents work in numbered steps. The one who later runs that plugin did not choose Lane, so is no user of it.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q1 step: "List each one who comes to the product with a goal of their own, a person or an AI, by the role they play."

decisions.what: Which plugins may the document name?
decisions.decided: Lane and the example plugin changelog only.
grounds: Lane depends on no plugin (steering T49).

decisions.what: How many objectives, and cut by what?
decisions.decided: Two: the rules of each step kept (O1), and the subagents started in the order the developer AI set (O2). A plugin can have rules without an order, or an order without rules, so each piece of work brings one of them closer.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q2 step: "Merge objectives that one piece of work would bring closer together."

decisions.what: O1, as one line with the user as its subject and no mechanism
decisions.decided: O1: The developer AI has its plugin's subagents keep the rules of their steps on every run, without writing checks. A rule is a sentence in a step that the subagent must keep, defined in the line after.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q1 step: "Write each one's objective as one sentence that fits on one line ... with no feature or mechanism of the product."

decisions.what: O2, as one line with the user as its subject and no mechanism
decisions.decided: O2: The developer AI has its plugin's subagents started in the order it set, on every run, without writing code for the order. The order it sets, its routes, is shown in O2's scenario.

decisions.what: What does each key result count?
decisions.decided: For each objective, a share of what the subagents do on runs that goes wrong, counted out of a named whole, then the lead time from the first rules or routes to the first run that keeps them. Lower and shorter are better.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q3 step: "Turn the signs kept into two measures: one of how well the user gets what the objective says, and the lead time"

decisions.decided: KR1.1: of the subagents' tool calls and ends of their work, the share that goes wrong: a broken rule that goes through, a broken rule stopped and then done another way, or an allowed call that is stopped. KR1.2: the lead time from the first rule for a plugin to the first run whose subagents keep the rules.

KR2.1: of the plugin's runs, the share that goes wrong: a subagent started that the routes do not name, or a start the routes name that is stopped. KR2.2: the lead time from the first routes for a plugin to the first run that keeps them.

decisions.what: How does the developer weigh a change that shortens the lead time?
decisions.decided: Said once under the OKRs: the first key result of each objective comes first, and the second is shortened only by a change that keeps the first. Key results have no target values (Goodhart's law).
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q4 thinking: "Quality first, then lead time"

decisions.what: Which plugin do the scenarios run on?
decisions.decided: changelog, which writes a project's CHANGELOG.md: lead starts the others, writer writes the new entries, reviewer compares them with the commits.
grounds: The README's walkthrough runs the same plugin.

decisions.what: Who takes part, and of what kind?
decisions.decided: developer AI (AI); Lane (script), one box for all Lane gives, as its scripts are inside the product; lead, writer and reviewer (AI). No step waits for a person.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q6 step: "every message's sender and receiver is named there"

decisions.what: What does the document show, and what does it leave to the architecture?
decisions.decided: Only what the developer AI does, sees and receives, and what its subagents do in its sight. Lane's scripts, the words they tell lead and how they check each call are inside the box, left to the README and the architecture.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q7 thinking: "the document says only what users mean to do, see and receive"

decisions.what: How much does a step of a scenario say?
decisions.decided: Each arrow says in a few words what one does to another. The content passed, such as the rules or the routes, is the spec, left to the README and Lane's docs.
grounds: A label that holds the content crowds the diagram, and the reader cannot follow the steps at a glance (the user, 2026-11-04).

decisions.decided: By its objective's ID and a short active phrase, the developer AI its subject: "O1: The developer AI holds writer to two rules", "O2: The developer AI has lead start writer and reviewer in its order".
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q5 step: "Name each scenario by its objective's ID and a short active verb phrase"

decisions.what: Do the subagents run in the foreground or in the background?
decisions.decided: In the background, so the developer AI's conversation stays free while they run.
grounds: dev/plugin-best-practice.md, Messages: Roles run in the background.

decisions.decided: The developer AI gives Lane two rules for writer's steps, sees the steps as they will read, and approves them. Lane writes them. The developer AI starts writer, and writer ends with both rules kept.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q5 step: "the first message is the user's request, the last gives the user the end"

decisions.decided: The developer AI gives Lane the routes, sees the routes and the steps as they will read, and approves them. Lane writes them. The developer AI starts lead. In a loop until reviewer ends with good, lead starts writer and then reviewer, as the routes say. lead ends with the reviewed entries.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/ux.json Q5 step: "Mark a part that repeats as a loop with its condition"
